title: Gangsters and the clubs: Capone's brother and Walter Barnes
summary: He worked for Capone's brother Ralph and Ed Fox, recalls Walter Barnes and his fatal tour, and says known gangsters frequented the clubs.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Did you ever see Big Jim Coliseum around?
I saw him. Yeah, I saw him in his place, but I don't remember seeing him in one of those places.
He didn't come around to him. He might have.

You didn't see him? No, I didn't know him until later on, you know. Yeah, it was maybe a year or so before he was killed, assassinated. But he could have, and I worked for it. I worked for Capone's brother, Ralph. Yeah, the syndicate had the grand tier, so the Hood Heinz bands. A fellow by the name of Fox, Ed Fox, was the front and the manager I'd say. And so I worked for him. And then his brother had a place called Cotton Club. The late Walter Barnes played there sometimes too. He's a fellow that brought up in Natchez.
Yeah, where was he from, anyhow, really?
Well, when I first knew Walter, he was in Chicago.

So I couldn't say just where he was from. But I played with him, two engagements before he'd taken that ill-fated tour. And the Providence Hospital had some kind of benefit. And it was another club, it was a large club. And so he hired me for the two engagements. Well, he didn't ask me to make the trip, and I didn't want to go. I didn't ask him to go either, because I just figured he wasn't going to pay me the money I'd like to have. So when he was burned up in the fire and some of his men, naturally, when I was taking the picture of the band doing these two engagements, there I was in the picture. So I was denying I was dead for about a couple of months. I thought you had burned him. No, I'm still alive and breathing, you know, one of those things. Yeah.
What about Johnny Torrio? Did you ever see him? Johnny Torrio?
If I did, I didn't know him. Yeah. You see what I'm talking about? Because in these places, it was known gangsters that frequented the places. They were there?
They were in there every night, yeah.
